label: paragraph_title
text: HONGKONG, MONDAY, OCTOBER 5, 1925.

label: paragraph_title
text: SWATOW POSITION.

label: text
text: EXPORT EMBARGO ON FOOD.

label: text
text: LATEST NEWS FROM PORT.

label: text
text: At present Swatow has an embargo on the export of food-stuffs from that port. It is not known if the embargo is being enforced as a result of the temporary regulations issued by the new authorities, or as part of the anti-foreign movement.

label: text
text: Chinese merchants who returned yesterday on the "Hydrangea" state that business conditions are returning to normal, and the situation is quiet. When the ship sailed, a number of men boarded the ship to search for foodstuffs but the speaker did not know if they were from labour unions or were empowered by the Government.

label: text
text: The "Hydrangea" brought back general cargo and a good many passengers.

label: paragraph_title
text: CADETS PAY $3,000.

label: text
text:
COMPENSATION FOR KILLE
JAPANESE.

label: text
text: WHAMPOA RIVER SEQUEL

label: text
text: Compensation is reported to have been paid by the Canton Government in respect of the Japanese sailor who was killed by the Whampoa Cadets firing at a Japanese vessel, from the shore, on July 30.

label: text
text: For the dead man, $3,000 was offered and $500 each for the two men wounded, so it is stated, on a protest being made by the Japanese Consul at Canton, and following representations.

label: paragraph_title
text: UNRULY CONDUCT.

label: text
text:
WEST INDIANS
CONVICTED.

label: text
text: ASSAULT CHARGE FAILS.

label: text
text: Charges of disorderly conduct and assaulting a Chinese detective were preferred against four West Indians at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning.

label: text
text: The evidence showed that a small girl had thrown some rubbish out of a window which alighted on a Chinese passer-by. The latter remonstrated and was assaulted by one of the defendants. Later at Hunghom Police Station they were alleged to have created a disturbance and threatened the detective.

label: text
text: Charge of disorderly conduct only was proved and the men were fined $25 each.

label: text
text: On the allegation of throwing rubbish, the small girl was let off. the complainant's evidence being said to be conflicting.

label: paragraph_title
text: COLLISION ENQUIRY.

label: text
text: The court of enquiry into the circumstances attending a collision between the s.s. "Talthybius" and a fishing boat will sit on Friday, October 9 at 10.30 instead of Wednesday, as previously announced.

label: text
text: The composition of the court is as follows: Commander C. R. H. Harvey, R.N., Superintendent; Charts Depot; Capt. T. Croft (s.s. "Mausang"), Capt. P. Gill (s.s. "Haifoong"), Capt. Shearen (s.s. "Halvard").

label: paragraph_title
text: ALLEGED BRIBERY.

label: text
text: MOTOR CAR DRIVER CHARGED.

label: text
text: A Chinese motor car driver was charged at the Central Magistracy this morning with leaving his car unattended and offering a bribe of $1 to an Indian constable.

label: text
text:
The constable stated in evidence that he saw the motor car left at Queen's Road Central yesterday without an attendant. The driver returned later and was informed that he would be summoned. The money was then forced into his pocket with a request to keep it and have a drink.
The case was reminded, ball being allowed on 360.
TODAY'S DOLLAR

label: text
text: STOCK EXCHANGE REPORT PREMATURE

label: text
text: LOCAL OPINION.

label: text
text: The report which appeared a few days ago that the Hongkong Stock Exchange was to open this morning was not correct, the contrary decision having been reached as a result of a meeting of the Exchange, a “China Mail” representative was informed upon enquiry to-day.

label: text
text: The consensus of opinion in Ice House Street seems to be that although there has lately been appreciably increased movement in shares, the volume of business and prices fetched are not sufficient to justify opening the market. The broking community are awaiting the announcement of the lines of administration by the Hongkong Government of the loan from Home and hopes run high of a policy in favour of advances upon local share securities which, it is thought, would considerably relieve the situation, particularly from the point of view of some of the native banks who are said to be asking clients for more margin on share securities.

label: text
text: Interesting, as indicating, a faith in Hongkong, is the report of a broker who told a “China Mail” representative that much of the buying of local shares of the last week emanated from the outports, Straits Settlements, etc.

label: text
text: An official of the Stock Exchange told the reporter that although the report of an opening had been premature such opening of the Stock Exchange would not, in his opinion, be long delayed.

label: paragraph_title
text: GAMBLING CHARGE.

label: text
text: CHINESE ROULETTE IN COURT.

label: text
text: A QWER WITNESS

label: text
text: A Northern Chinese who entered the witness box at the Central Magistracy this morning to give evidence on behalf of a man charged with gambling created an amusing scene by making it appear that he had come to a theatrical performance. The interpreter reprimand-ed him at which he laughed all the more, and he made a hurried exit from the box after repeating a few words of the oath. Repeated efforts were made to bring the man to realise his surroundings, but they had no effect, and the Magistrate Mr. S. B. B. McElderry ordered him to leave the Court.

label: text
text: In the case of the man who was charged with keeping a rotlette table, Divisiona Inspector Ogg stated that the accused was convicted and fined $5 on Saturday for the same offence, when the apparatus was returned to him.

label: text
text: A Chinese detective stated in evidence that he came upon a crowd of people round a table on which was placed the roulette apparatus. The stakes were one cent pieces, and the winners received five cents or a packet of cigarettes. When accosted by witness, the accused offered him a packet of cigarettes as a bribe.

label: text
text: The case was adjourned until tomorrow for further enquiries.

label: paragraph_title
text: SUSPECT ARRESTED.

label: paragraph_title
text: MURDER OF INDIAN CONSTABLE..

label: text
text: KOWLOON CITY INCIDENT.

label: text
text: The murder of an Indian constable at Ngau Shi Wan on July 8 was recalled at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning when a Chinese was formally charged with the crime and remanded for one week.

label: text
text: It will be remembered that the constable was detailed to watch a man who had been caught with stolen firewood whilst other officers went up the hillside. On their return they found the constable lying on the ground with bullet wounds, and he died in hospital. A search for the assailant has resulted in the arrest of the man now charged with murder.

label: paragraph_title
text: STRIKERS KILLED?

label: text
text: CHINESE HOSTILITY TO PICKETS.

label: text
text: FARMER USES HIS POLE.

label: text
text: Reports of 'open hostility, and the loss of life in at least one instance, between Chinese strike pickets and the civil population, have reached Hongkong during the week-end.

label: paragraph_title
text: THREE STRIKERS KILLED?

label: text
text: (An Occasional Correspondent.)

label: text
text: Mácao, October 4.

label: text
text: It is reported from Chinshan that strike pickets had the worse of a brawl with farmers in Chinese territory, resulting in the death of three strikers.

label: text
text: Early yesterday morning, a farmer was stated to be coming into Macao with vegetables. On nearing the border he was challenged by pickets. He threw down his two baskets and moved away. On three men of the picket coming up, he belaboured them with his bamboo pole until all three were badly bruised and unable to stand. Even with the pickets down, the farmer is alleged to have continued the assault until, so it is stated, life was extinct in each case. None of the pickets was armed.

label: paragraph_title
text: Shots: Fired.

label: text
text: In the district of Po On (which adjoins the New Territory) trouble is believed to have broken out between armed tickets and the farmers' volunteers. Feeling has been running him for some time owing to the prompt of export of products to trongkong and consequent consscation.

label: text
text: Firing is said to have broken out between the rival factibns.

label: paragraph_title
text: Canton Incident.

label: text
text: A passenger who returned on Saturday by the "Honam" relates an incident which he witnessed on the West Bund.

label: text
text: He says that among the food-stuffs sent up to Shameen from Hongkong was beef, in quarters, the dripping of which was cut off and often thrown into the river. Some of the very poor Chinese are said to have dived in the river for the dripping. On going ashore the divers were caught by strike pickets who set upon the divers for picking up cast-off food. One man was tied up on the Bund and beaten for half an hour.

label: paragraph_title
text: SOVIET CITIZENS.

label: text
text: CONDITIONS OF RECENT AMNESITY.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Mo-cow, Oct. 4

label: text
text: The council of Commissaries has issued a decree that former prisons of war and interned persons of the old Imperial and Red armies, also participants in risings of White armies who come under conditions of the, amnesty shall lose their citizenship if they neglect to apply for restoration of citizenship within the period laid down by the decree.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHEUNG CHAU NOTES

label: text
text: This did not apply to persons who have not renewed their citizenship owing to lack of Soviet representatives in the country of their residence.

label: text
text: The local Government boys' school has been re-opened and seems to be well attended. A school for the younger members of the Missionary families was started yesterday (Friday) in house No. 15. Under ordinary conditions the youngsters would be at work in Canton at this time.

label: text
text: A change in the launch time table has been made as from yesterday. Intending day, or week-end visitors should take note.

label: text
text:

label: paragraph_title
text: BLIND HOME.

label: text
text: LADY POLLOCK'S PRAISE

label: text
text: There was a large attendance at St. John's Cathedral Hall this morning, when a sale of work in aid of the Kowloon Home for the Blind was opened.

label: text
text: The proceedings began by the girls of the Home singing a hymn accompanied by their orchestra under Mr. S. Paul. A prayer was offered by the Rev. T. B. Powell, and the sale was then opened by Lady Pollock.

label: text
text: Lady Pollock made a graceful speech in which she called attention to the admirable work done by Miss Beswick, who was in charge of the Home, and the excellence of the work turned out by the scholars. She said that although we could not speak their language, and so could hardly express our thanks, the scholars were so susceptible of influence that they would realise how sympathetic we were to them in their affliction. She congratulated the scholars on their singing and playing, and also thanked Mr. Paul for the great interest he displayed in the work of the Home.

label: text
text: There were a number of stalls on which were displayed table covers, embroideries, knitted work and other articles which had been done by the blind inmates. All the articles were skillfully executed, and so excellent has been the work of the scholars that several parcels have already been sent to the Wembley Exhibition.

label: text
text: The sale will continue until 6 o'clock this evening. Amongst the ladies assisting at the stalls are Mesdames Blanchett. Gerken, Hailey-Bell, Wood, Hegarty, Noll and Arrowsmith.

label: paragraph_title
text: PEACE DELEGATES:

label: text
text: MERCHANTS RETURNING TO HONGKONG.

label: text
text: NO CONCRETE PROPOSAL.

label: text
text: No proposal that can be described as concrete has been put forward as the result of Hongkong delegation of Chinese merchants to Canton.

label: text
text: Some of the delegates returned yesterday and others are due back this week. They are to prepare a document reporting their activities in Canton, such as reporting the District Commercial Associations — the general guild having sponsored the peace delegation—to be held at 7 p.m. tomorrow.

label: text
text: Summed up briefly the position is that the delegates desired to confine themselves to asking for communication to be resumed whereas the Canton Strike Executive wished to include in the discussion a number of points that can hardly be called relevant.

label: text
text: Unless an improvement results from the conference (in Canton) of last night, it is difficult to see where a. settlement is going to start.

label: text
text: The strikers are reported to have put forward terms, in addition to those published last week, such as the free use of Chinese subsidiary coin in Hongkong, the liberty of deported strikers to return. etc.

label: paragraph_title
text: ABERDEEN SHOP.

label: paragraph_title
text: SUBJECT OF LEGAL PROCEEDINGS.

label: text
text: An arrangement entered into between a tenant firm of premises at 57 Main Street, Aberdeen, and another firm by which the latter firm entered into possession formed the subject of proceedings at the Summary Court this morning.

label: text
text:
The question for the Court to decide was whether the document drawn up between these parties was an assignment. His Lordship said that the landlord must have known what was going on as the change was advertised in the newspapers and posters were exhibited in the window of the shop.

label: paragraph_title
text: MALARIA SCOURGE

label: text
text: INTERNATIONAL CONGRESS OPENS.

label: text
text: The inaugural meeting of the International Congress on malaria has opened at the Capitol.

label: text
text: The Premier, M. Mussolini, and a large number of international experts, on malaria were present, including representatives from Burma, India and the Malay States.

label: text
text: Signor Mussolini paid a high tribute to Britain and her dominions for their striking example and collaboration in fighting the scourge of malaria.

label: text
text: The Argentine delegate proposed the establishment of an international anti-malaria institute at Rome to collect worldwide information and to undertake research work for the redemption of infected regions and to organise practical teaching for the training of malaria specialists.

label: text
text: The Italian delegate promised that Italy would support the proposal and was ready to provide building and supply funds towards "be organisation of an institute.

label: text
text: The Congress approved the proposal and entrusted its council to draw up a scheme.
